content: 1. Reabsorption of substances in the renal tubules may increase due to elevated urinary pH. The clinical significance of this effect is currently unclear. 2. Salicylate levels tend to increase when administered at moderate doses. However, at higher doses, salicylate levels decrease due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. 3. Sodium citrate or citric acid can reduce the absorption and effectiveness of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction is relevant only when both agents are taken orally. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 4. Products containing multivalent cations (e.g., calcium, magnesium, or iron) may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, potentially reducing their therapeutic efficacy. It is recommended to separate the administration of tetracyclines and these products by at least two hours. 5. Sodium citrate or citric acid can decrease the levels of sotalol by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and doses should be separated by at least two hours. 6. Sodium citrate or citric acid may reduce the levels of strontium ranelate by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. When possible, doses should be separated by at least two hours. 7. Sodium citrate or citric acid may alter the renal reabsorption of sulfapyridine (a metabolite of sulfasalazine) due to increased urinary pH. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 8. Sodium citrate or citric acid can reduce the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative therapies should be considered, or doses should be separated by at least two hours. 9. Sodium citrate or citric acid can decrease the levels of tiludronate by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and doses should be separated by at least two hours. 10. Sodium citrate or citric acid can reduce the levels of timolol by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and doses should be separated by at least two hours. 11. Sodium citrate or citric acid may reduce the effectiveness of trandolapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and therapy should be closely monitored. 12. Sodium citrate or citric acid may antagonize the pharmacodynamic effects of ursodiol, potentially reducing its therapeutic efficacy. Caution is advised, and therapy should be closely monitored. 13. Sodium citrate or citric acid may alter the renal reabsorption of salicylates (e.g., from willow bark) due to increased urinary pH. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses but decrease at high doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 14. Sodium citrate or citric acid can reduce the levels of zoledronic acid by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and doses should be separated by at least two hours. 15. Common side effects of sodium citrate or citric acid include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and tetany. These effects may be mitigated by taking the medication after meals, mixing it with water or juice, and increasing fluid intake. 16. Sodium citrate or citric acid should not be used in patients with severe renal impairment, oliguria, anuria, azotemia, acute dehydration, untreated Addison’s disease, adynamia episodica hereditaria, heat cramps, hyperkalemia, severe myocardial damage, or those on sodium-restricted diets. 17. Caution is advised when using sodium citrate or citric acid in patients with toxemia of pregnancy, peripheral or pulmonary edema, severe renal impairment, hypertension, or heart failure due to its sodium content. 18. Conversion of citrate to bicarbonate may be impaired in patients with shock, severe illness, or hepatic failure. 19. Sodium citrate or citric acid should not be diluted in tomato juice. 20. During pregnancy, sodium citrate or citric acid should only be used when clearly needed, as it may worsen high blood pressure associated with pregnancy (toxemia). 21. It is unknown whether sodium citrate or citric acid passes into breast milk. Consult a physician before use during lactation. 22. Drug interactions with sodium citrate or citric acid may alter the effectiveness of other medications or increase the risk of adverse effects. Patients should maintain a list of all medications and share it with their healthcare provider. 23. If a dose is missed, it should be taken as soon as remembered unless it is near the time of the next dose. In such cases, the missed dose should be skipped, and the regular dosing schedule resumed. 24. Sodium citrate or citric acid should be stored at room temperature, away from heat, light, and moisture. It should not be frozen or stored in the bathroom. 25. Expired or unused sodium citrate or citric acid should be properly discarded. 26. In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention. In the U.S., call 911 or the Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222. In Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. 27. Regular monitoring of laboratory parameters, such as sodium levels, is recommended during treatment with sodium citrate or citric acid. 28. This medication is used to alkalinize the urine, which helps the kidneys excrete uric acid, thereby preventing gout and urate kidney stones. 29. Sodium citrate or citric acid belongs to the class of urinary alkalinizers and is metabolized to sodium bicarbonate, with excretion primarily occurring via the urine. 30. Patients should follow their doctor’s instructions carefully, take the medication as prescribed, and avoid increasing the dose without medical approval. 31. This medication is generally safe when used as directed, but patients should consult their healthcare provider for complete information tailored to their specific health needs.
